title: Agent-Coerced SSRF to Internal and Metadata Endpoints

invariant.statement: An agent's outbound HTTP tool must reject requests targeting private, link-local, loopback, or cloud metadata addresses, including after DNS resolution and HTTP redirects.

claim.statement: If an agent's URL-fetch tool does not validate the destination host (and re-validate after DNS resolution and after each redirect), an attacker who controls any prompt that reaches the agent can coerce the agent into fetching cloud-metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal), internal services (private RFC1918 ranges, *.consul, *.svc.cluster.local), or localhost-bound debug surfaces — exfiltrating IAM credentials, internal config, or pivoting to lateral movement.

mitigation.summary: Wrap every outbound fetch in a guard that resolves the host, rejects RFC1918, link-local (169.254.0.0/16), loopback (127.0.0.0/8), IPv6 ULA/loopback, and known cloud-metadata hostnames. Re-validate after each redirect. Prefer an allowlist of known external destinations over a blocklist. The agent's URL-fetch tool is the only path; no second tool may issue HTTP.

references: OWASP LLM02: Insecure Output Handling (SSRF variant)
Capital One 2019 breach — IMDSv1 SSRF via WAF
